key_insight: In this retrospective comparison, modified Morrow myectomy produced more complete 1-year LVOT gradient reduction, while Liwen ablation had fewer conduction disturbances and shorter recovery metrics.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest a trade-off between stronger hemodynamic relief and lower conduction-system risk when choosing between these two obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy procedures.
method: 211 treated patients overall; 133 had 1-year serial follow-up
Repeated measures analyzed with linear mixed-effects models and generalized estimating equations, adjusted for baseline covariates
evidence_signal: At 1 year, adjusted LVOT gradient remained higher after Liwen than myectomy (16.1 vs 1.3 mmHg), but new conduction abnormalities were much lower with Liwen (5% vs 62%).
watch_item: Because this was a nonrandomized, single-center retrospective study, treatment selection bias and limited generalizability may affect how confidently the results can guide practice.
paper_title: Liwen Ablation versus Modified Morrow Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Hemodynamic and Conduction Outcomes
